outcome: Hear the room on the wall: the music you play, drawn as it sounds.

views.title: Now playing
views.condition: Set music_visual: spectrum or level in Ramka 0.4.0 and mark one board music: true; without a reading the strip falls back to the classic wave.
views.layout: Ramka landscape layout: 1024–1280 × 720–800 CSS px; phone/portrait dashboard not claimed.

setup: Flash the M5Stack Atom EchoS3R over USB the first time with the device file the component writes; later updates go over Wi-Fi.
Adopt the board in Home Assistant through ESPHome and map its entities in the component's inputs.
Calibrate the sound level against a reference meter, or keep the offset marked as an estimate.
To see it on the tablet, set Ramka's music_visual and choose the look on the Ramka settings dashboard.

states.label: Music
states.headline: The strip follows the music
states.detail: Fictional values: the third-octave spectrum from the board, about five updates a second.

states.label: Quiet
states.headline: A calm room
states.detail: The level is reported every second, unweighted; the offset turns dBFS into dB SPL.

states.label: Offline
states.headline: Back to the classic wave
states.detail: While the board has no reading, the now-playing strip shows the classic wave.
